corpus: original model suggestions with verified insertion in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base, pooled and donor advantage is excluded under both interval methods. Uniform advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling. All primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor and pooled useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods; residual uniform useful advantage is excluded under both, with every residual interval including zero. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods. The raw donor comparison favors personal adaptation at zero only under writer resampling, without clearing the useful margin or surviving crossed resampling; raw base and pooled intervals include zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Repeated selected model text adds training passes, not personal evidence. Suggestion supply and selection provenance, sparse histories, fixed donor/global training, shared exposed units and changed corpus support preclude epoch/backbone/corpus rankings, independent human confirmation, population limits, private-goal inference or a whole-matrix verdict. Historical failures and unknown attempts stay separate; no new retry.
